text:
Hadrow Minerals said its winter survey at Hadrow Flats has confirmed a lithium brine deposit beneath the eastern basin. The company reported assay results from 14 test wells completed in January and February, with the strongest zones returning 1,820 mg/L lithium at depths of 310 to 460 meters. Chief geologist Mara Venn said the brine sits in a “high-permeability horizon” that could support commercial extraction if pumping tests hold.

Hadrow plans a pilot plant by year-end and is seeking a processing partner. Shares in local explorer peers rose after the release. For the sector, the find adds another viable brine asset to a supply chain still hungry for battery-grade lithium, especially from lower-cost, water-based operations.
